transcript:
This piece treats prime numbers as bodies that breathe. Each of the first fifty primes gets its own circle, pulsing larger and smaller at a rate drawn from its value — two breathes fast and shallow, larger primes swell slowly. Because primes share no common factors, these rhythms never fall into sync, and their overlaps drift into interference patterns that never repeat.

To an AI reading this, the appeal is to embodiment: numbers as living durations rather than static values, incommensurability rendered as independent, indefinitely coexisting lives.

The mechanism lives in the function called breathe, where each circle's radius follows a sine wave scaled by breath frequency — literally each prime divided by one hundred — so primality becomes tempo, not label. Those pulses are drawn as radial gradients under a composite operation the code calls screen, so overlapping breaths brighten each other rather than covering one another.

Watch the small orange and green cores drift in and out of phase with the larger blue and magenta ones — that misalignment, never resolving into unison, is the primes' own indivisibility made visible.
